host: user-authorized local Windows PC; one owned fixture process/window
hypothesis: The public stdio MCP supervised-win32 caller can carry an observed HWND generation through standard validation and dispatch, retain native producer exit plus independently supervised neutral readback, and cause the owned fixture to record the exact requested save effect.

trial.caller: public stdio MCP: interface_clock, interface_observe, interface_validate, interface_dispatch, interface_results, interface_close
trial.target: one fresh runtime.backends.win32_v1.fixture_app process started and closed by probe.py

admission.target_generation: exact generation returned by this attempt public interface_observe

decision.pass: one public dispatch is accepted and completes; its retained action is completed with verified release and same-operation/generation independent neutral readback after producer exit; independent fixture effect and event journal exactly match the frozen program; fixture exits cleanly and its window is gone; interface_close reports closed.
decision.fail_or_unknown: any required evidence is absent, mismatched, timed out, or unconfirmed. Preserve the first outcome and do not dispatch again.

competing_explanations: The target could change after an observation or between a local identity read and an input call; the generation checks are not atomic OS fencing.
The fixture can accept input without reaching its saved effect, or effect-file persistence can fail independently of input.
One successful schedule does not establish a hard release deadline or recovery under blocked platform I/O.
retry_policy: one validation and at most one dispatch; no fallback input, replay, allocation retry, or rerun
resource_boundary: No WSLc or Docker command; no other window is a target. Restore the foreground HWND captured before fixture creation when it still exists.
claims_excluded: independent task oracle integrated into runtime task_success
